# DSH Session Share

Download a whole Session as one self-contained HTML file and send it to anyone.
The recipient can op

en it in a browser without DSH, an account, a server, or an
internet connection. If they also instal

l this plugin, they can import the file
back into DSH as a read-only chat view and continue it as a

, they can import the file
back into DSH as a read-only chat view and continue it as a real Session.

> **Status: source published, package unpublished.** The GitHub repository is
> public at <https://g

ithub.com/osman3n/dsh-session-share>, but the package is
> not on npm and is not listed on `awesome-

dsh-plugin.com` or `dsh-market`. It
> therefore has **0 stars** and no hub card. See

## What it changes
Two controls, no changes to existing chat rendering:

1. A 28 px share icon in the action row under each finalized assistant message â€”
immediately after

**Copy** and before **Like / Dislike** and **Branch**.
2. A 28 px import icon in the Workspaces hea

der, beside **Search**,
**View options**, and **Add workspace**.

The share icon exports the **whole Session**, not just that one reply, so every
reply offers the sam

e download. The import icon reads a DSH Session Share HTML
file and opens a read-only, chat-style tr

anscript in the central panel. Merely
opening it does not create a Session, add anything to your his

tory, or send the
imported text to a model. No other plugin is required.

The imported panel uses the same conversation width, right-aligned user
messages, plain assistant Ma

rkdown, and attachment cards as the normal chat.
Image and file attachments are shown by name, size,

and type; their bytes are
not embedded in the shared HTML. Tool output stays in compact collapsible

ype; their bytes are
not embedded in the shared HTML. Tool output stays in compact collapsible rows.

The imported panel has one explicit **Continue in a new chat** button. It creates
a real Session and

appends the imported turns to that Session's log, so the next
message continues the conversation wi

th the imported history in model context.
That action does send the imported text to the configured

model; it asks for
confirmation first. A workspace selector next to the button chooses where the
new

Session is created. It defaults to **Ungrouped**; pick a Workspace from the
list if you want the ne

. It defaults to **Ungrouped**; pick a Workspace from the
list if you want the new chat filed there.
## Install (suggested, not performed)

This repository is only the source. Installation is a separate, explicit step
for the person who wan

y is only the source. Installation is a separate, explicit step
for the person who wants the button:

1. Clone this repository, or use an existing checkout.
2. Open DSH's plugin manager for the current

profile and install the bundle from
the folder containing this README. On this machine that folder i

s
`C:\Users\osman_lam\Projects\Basic\plugins\session-share`.
3. Reload or restart DSH if the plugin
manager asks for it.

Do not install it merely to read this README. The built-in Session log export
already covers Markdow
n copy and ZIP download without any extra plugin.
## Use
### Share

1. Open a Session.
2. Click the share icon under any assistant reply.
3. The browser downloads `dsh-

session-<session-id>.html`.
4. Send that file. The recipient can open it directly, or import it if t

hey have
this plugin.
### Import

1. Click the import icon in the Workspaces header, next to Search and View
options.
2. Choose a `dsh

-session-*.html` file produced by this plugin.
3. The transcript opens in a read-only panel. Use **B
ack to chat** to return.

Only the inert JSON block embedded in the file is read; imported HTML scripts are
never executed, re

mote assets are never loaded, and merely importing adds no
Session to your history.

To continue it, leave the destination as **Ungrouped** or choose a Workspace in
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy

The export contains the committed Session transcript, including tool
arguments, command output, file

paths and anything else that was visible in the
Session. It can contain secrets. Review the HTML be

fore sending it, and treat
the file with the same care as the original conversation.

The Host route is authenticated by DSH's Connection service. There is no public
endpoint and no uplo

ad: the browser downloads the file locally. The continuation
route is also authenticated and accepts

only the small, validated transcript
payload; it never accepts a raw HTML page.

An imported transcript is untrusted input. Continuing it makes that text part of
the model's context

, where it could contain prompt-injection attempts or a
forged conversation. The confirmation dialog

exists for that reason. Do not
continue a file from someone you do not trust.

Do not enable this plugin in a profile that is exposed to people who should not
read the Sessions in

ot enable this plugin in a profile that is exposed to people who should not
read the Sessions in it.
## Compatibility

Built against the current DSH Session event format, the
`conversation.chat.assistant-actions` slot,

and the `main` keyed panel slot. The
share action uses a per-Session `inject(sessionId)` callback; t

he import action
uses the `layout` service to open a read-only panel without changing the current
Se

n
uses the `layout` service to open a read-only panel without changing the current
Session. It uses:

- `sessionQuery.readSession()` on the Host;
- `connection.fetch.register()` for the authenticated ro

n, and `sessions.flush()` before handing the id back;
- the client `slots`, `locale`, `layout`, `uiW

orkspace`, and `workspaces`
services;
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout` and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-cl
ient-ui-workspace` as declared client dependencies.

No DSH client packages are imported at runtime. The renderer is dependency-free.
The import button f

inds the Workspaces header by its stable `_headerActions`
suffix, so a future DSH redesign could mov

e or hide it; the rest of the feature
is slot-based.
## Why not LiveShare?

DSH ships an experimental official LiveShare plugin, but it shares a **live**
Session through a sepa

rately deployed Liveshare server, with owner OAuth and
server-issued credentials. It is not a static

transcript export and is not a
turnkey install. This plugin exists for the simpler case: send the h

istory to
someone who was not there.
